items.stem: Where should a team plan live, according to the module?

options.label: In the place your team already checks
Only in your head
In a private note no one sees

items.hint_text: A plan helps only when the team can see it.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Write the plan where the team already looks so they can see it.
items.feedback_wrong: A plan helps only when the team can see it, so write it where they already look. A plan kept in your head or a private note cannot be helped with.

items.stem: Which version of a plan can a team actually use?

options.label: A shared list with names and dates
A plan you remember and explain when asked
A rough feeling about who is busy

items.hint_text: Look for the plan anyone can check.
items.feedback_correct: Right. Names and dates let anyone spot a gap and offer help.
items.feedback_wrong: Names and dates let anyone spot a gap and offer help. A remembered plan or a vague feeling cannot be checked or shared.

items.stem: Which details make a plan visible and usable? Select all that apply.

options.label: Who is responsible for each task
When each task is due
A task list kept only in your memory
Where the team can read the plan

items.hint_text: A usable plan names owners, dates, and a place to read it.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Owners, due dates, and a shared place make the plan usable.
items.feedback_wrong: A usable plan names who does what, by when, in a place the team can read. Keeping the list only in your memory makes it invisible to everyone else.

items.stem: When is asking for help planning rather than an emergency?

options.label: Early, before the deadline nears
On the last day
After the deadline has passed

items.feedback_correct: Correct. Asking early gives people time to help and keeps the plan on track.
items.feedback_wrong: Asking early gives people time to help and keeps the plan on track. Asking on the last day or after the deadline turns help into an emergency.

items.stem: Which actions show a team leader asking for help in time? Select all that apply.

options.label: Flag a task at risk days before it is due
Ask a teammate to take one task early
Wait until the deadline to mention a problem
Hide the delay to look confident

items.hint_text: Asking early means raising a risk before it is urgent.
items.feedback_correct: Right. Flagging a risk and sharing work early are both asking in time.
items.feedback_wrong: Asking early means raising a risk and sharing work before it is urgent. Waiting until the deadline or hiding a delay removes the team's chance to help.

items.stem: Why write down who does what and by when?

options.label: So anyone can spot a gap and help
So you can keep it secret
So no one else needs to look

items.hint_text: A written plan is meant to be shared.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. A written plan is shared so the team can see gaps and offer help.
items.feedback_wrong: A written plan is shared so the team can see gaps and offer help. Keeping it secret or keeping others out defeats the purpose.

items.stem: A plan that lives only in your head has what problem?

options.label: It cannot be helped with
It is always more accurate
It saves everyone time

items.hint_text: No one else can see a plan in your head.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. If the plan is only in your head, no one else can see it or help with it.
items.feedback_wrong: If the plan is only in your head, no one else can see it or help with it. That does not make it more accurate or save the team time.

items.stem: Which plans can a team use? Select all that apply.

options.label: A shared list showing each task's owner
A schedule with due dates everyone can read
A plan you explain only when asked
A private guess about who is free

items.hint_text: A usable plan shows owners and dates where the team can read them.
items.feedback_correct: Right. A shared list of owners and a readable schedule are both usable.
items.feedback_wrong: A usable plan shows owners and due dates where the team can read them. A plan kept private or explained only on request stays invisible to the team.

items.stem: A task is behind schedule three days before it is due. What should you do?

options.label: Ask for help now
Wait and hope it catches up
Say nothing until it is due

items.hint_text: Earlier asking leaves time to help.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Asking three days early gives the team time to help and adjust.
items.feedback_wrong: Asking three days early gives the team time to help and adjust the plan. Waiting or staying silent turns a small risk into a missed deadline.

items.stem: Which sentence matches the module's view of asking for help?

options.label: Asking on Monday is planning, asking on Friday is an emergency.
Asking for help always looks weak.
A good leader never asks for help.

items.hint_text: The module frames early asking as planning.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. Early asking is planning; late asking is an emergency.
items.feedback_wrong: The module frames early asking as planning, not weakness. Leaders who never ask remove the team's ability to help before it is too late.
